PROJECT.TITLE: How the Project form works
PROJECT.INTRO: A Project links a Client, a Team (Mesa) and a Module. The Module decides which Task templates are reviewed in step 2 before the tickets are generated.
PROJECT.STEP2: In step 2, review each task: pick a Category (required - every ticket must have one), an assignee, a due date and, optionally, a scheduled date.
PROJECT.AFTER: Once confirmed, one ticket is created per task, linked to this Project. The Project cannot be marked as Finalizado while any of its tickets is still open.

MODULE.TITLE: How Modules work
MODULE.INTRO: A Module is a named bundle of Task templates (e.g. "Standard onboarding"). Creating a Project with a Module attaches all of its tasks at once, in the order shown here.
MODULE.SHORTCUT: Use the shortcut on the Project form to create a new Module without losing what you were filling in - it opens in a new tab.

TASK.TITLE: How Task templates work
TASK.INTRO: A Task template defines what a generated ticket looks like: its default title, description, default assignee, days until due, and which Project stage it advances to when completed.
TASK.CHECKLIST: Attach a ready-made Checklist to require specific information before the ticket can be resolved. Only required items block completion.

CHECKLIST.TITLE: How Checklist items work
CHECKLIST.INTRO: Each item has a type: Checkbox (a plain yes/no), Text, Single choice (pick one of your own options) or Value (a number).
CHECKLIST.REQUIRED: Mark an item as Required to make it block the ticket's completion until it is filled in or checked - optional items are informational only.

TUTORIAL.TITLE: Projects tutorial
TUTORIAL.STEP1: 1. Create the Task templates you'll reuse (Settings → Projects → Tasks). Each one defines the default ticket title, due days and, optionally, a Checklist.
TUTORIAL.STEP2: 2. Group related tasks into a Module (Settings → Projects → Modules) - e.g. "Standard onboarding" with Initial contact, Installation, Training.
TUTORIAL.STEP3: 3. Create a Project, pick the Client, the Team and that Module. Step 2 lets you review the assignee, category and dates of every task before confirming.
TUTORIAL.STEP4: 4. Confirming generates one ticket per task, already linked to the Project and to the Team's Kanban board.
TUTORIAL.STEP5: 5. As tickets are resolved, the Project can advance automatically to the next stage (configured per task). It can only reach Finalizado once every ticket is done.
TUTORIAL.STEP6: 6. Track total hours logged (Apontamento) and progress right on the Project card and detail view.
